Lesson 12: Present, reflect and review evidence

Visual Arts 1.2 · AS91913 v4 · 50 minutes · Teacher plan

Teacher / class: Date:

Learning intention

Present the resolved painting and explain the decisions that communicate its idea.

Students are learning to

  • Present the single painting with its title and clear identification.
  • Use visible evidence to explain selected conventions and technical decisions.

Materials & preparation

Prepare a dry, safe display space and photography setup if used. Confirm the school’s evidence, authenticity and moderation procedures. Bring process records and the student task sheet; gather reflection responses without imposing an extra assessment threshold.

Language to make visible

Presentation · reflection · authenticity · acknowledgement

Support & access

Offer an oral reflection or scribed access arrangement where appropriate. Use a clear presentation checklist and accessible viewing options.

Extend the learning

Compare the starting intention with the final painting and explain how a significant decision changed the communicated meaning.

Class adjustments

The Painting Room · 1.2 · Lesson 12 · Teaching brief 1 of 2

Lesson 12: classroom sequence

Present, reflect and review evidence · 50 minutes, including clean-up

Lesson 12 timed teaching sequence
Time / phaseTeaching and learning
0–5 minConnectStudents check that their work is dry, identified and ready to be viewed. Revisit the initial intention.
5–13 minTeach & modelModel a concise reflection that points to a particular painted passage, names a technical choice and explains its contribution. Clarify the locally agreed presentation and source-acknowledgement process.
13–38 minStudio practiceStudents title and present the single painting, document it as required locally and prepare a short written or oral reflection. Keep sources and progress studies available to support process and authenticity. View peers’ work respectfully.
38–45 minReview & checkStudents share one choice that communicates the idea and one future learning goal. Teacher checks completeness and authentic process; make assessment judgements separately against the official standard and normal moderation procedures.
45–50 minRecord & clean upCollect or record the agreed evidence, return resources and leave display and storage areas ready for the next class.

Check for learning

The final resolved painting, with locally agreed identification and supporting process records available.

Before the next lesson

Assess the substantial final artwork holistically. Use current NZQA guidance to calibrate judgements; reflect on teaching needs for the next unit.
